newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek state plans to float OTE - markets.
newsitem.headline: Greek state plans to float OTE - markets.

text.p: Market talk that Greece's socialist government plans to sell soon a second minority stake in state OTE telecom has prompted various flotation scenarios but both the state and OTE remain tight-lipped.

National economy ministry officials told Reuters that OTE's administration was currently examining different scenarios for the sale and it was possible that a final choice would surface in the next 10 days.
"We should have news in about 10 days," a ministry official said.
OTE officials were unavailable for comment.
With Greek stocks rallying in January, some market sources expected a stake of between 7 and 12 percent of OTE to be floated on the Athens Stock Exchange soon.

"There seems to be two scenarios for this sale: one through the flotation of existing shares and another through a share capital increase. I believe the first scenario is more likely," said Constantine Panagidis, general manager at Axon Securities.
The stake will probably be closer to the smallest percentage, seven to eight percent, he added.

Other financial analysts speculated the government would want to speed up the sale of another minority stake, originally planned for the end of 1997, and time it to coincide with an upbeat bourse sentiment.
They said foreign banks were expressing a particular interest in OTE shares already on the market.

In March 1996 the government launched a 6.034 percent float for OTE shares in a public offer to raise 80 billion drachmas, at the price of 4,000 drachmas each. Twenty million ordinary registered shares were offered for sale.
Another four million shares were sold to the oversubscribed staff and pensioners' placement for 16 billion drachmas.

Two attempts to partly privatise the near-monopoly OTE telecom fell through in 1993 and 1994 under conservative and socialist governments with elections, strikes and a weak bourse contributing to failure.
